Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Intake Brief: Challenges as achievements — sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements

## Problem statement

The engine's challenge system (per-run meta-goals, e.g. Main Street's "Foodie Row") is conceptually a form of achievement. Once the Steam version exists (Electron launcher with Steamworks), challenge completions should sync to Steam achievements so players earn persistent, account-level recognition visible on their Steam profile and in the overlay.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn Steam achievements for completing in-game challenges; see progress on their Steam profile.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — an engine-generic achievement layer so any game can map its challenges to Steam achievements without writing Steam SDK code.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want the challenges I complete in Main Street (and future games) to appear as Steam achievements, so my progress is recognised beyond the run itself.
- As a TCE developer, I want a game-agnostic achievement layer in the engine, so adding achievements to a new game is declarative (challenge → achievement mapping) with no Steam SDK code in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An **engine-generic achievement layer** exists in the core engine (extending the existing generic `ChallengeSystem` model): games define achievement definitions (id, title, description, hidden flag) and map challenge completions to achievements. This layer is pure engine code with no Steam dependency (works headless / in the web build).
2. When a challenge is completed inside the Steam launcher, the mapped Steam achievement is unlocked via Steamworks (`ISteamUserStats::SetAchievement` + `StoreStats`); verified by automated tests with a mocked Steamworks session and a documented manual E2E check with a real Steam account.
3. Steam sync is **idempotent and offline-safe**: unlocked achievements persist locally, are re-synced to Steam when available, and the launcher never crashes when Steam/Steamworks is absent (graceful degradation, consistent with the follow-on-Steam feature CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
4. A single **achievement manifest** (game id ↔ achievement id ↔ Steam API name, hidden flag) is the source of truth and matches the static Steam store configuration; mismatch detection is documented.
5. **Main Street is the first consumer**: all 12 challenge templates (`MainStreetChallenges.ts`) are mapped to Steam achievements through the generic layer (no Steam SDK code in the game module).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Timing:** Steam sync is implemented only when the Steam version exists — blocked by the Electron launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) and the Steamworks integration introduced by the follow-on-Steam incentive (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC). The engine-generic achievement layer itself can be designed/built now; the Steam bridge lands with Steamworks.
- **Engine-generic (user decision):** no game-specific Steam code; games declare achievements via the generic layer; Main Street first.
- **Steam backend reality:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steam store backend with static API names (App ID + achievement list). The manifest must match that configuration; store setup itself lives outside this repo.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies (Steamworks SDK usage follows the pattern set by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` / `ActiveChallengeRecord<TState>` interfaces plus generic selection/evaluation; game-agnostic by design ("M6 extraction" notes already anticipate reuse).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — the only consumer: 12 challenge templates across 5 categories, per-run selection (`selectChallenges`), evaluation with completion callback that pushes to `state.challengesCompleted` and the activity log. Challenges are run-local and non-persistent.
- No achievements, no Steam SDK code, no Electron code in the repo today. Steamworks integration is being introduced by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC into the launcher from CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC explicitly defers this scope: "Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item."

## Desired change

1. Add an **achievement concept to the core engine** (new module, e.g. `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`, or an extension of `ChallengeSystem`): achievement definitions, a completion-event surface, and a persistence-agnostic "unlock" registry that the web build can use without Steam.
2. Define the **achievement manifest** for the launcher (`electron/steam-achievements.ts`): game/achievement ids ↔ Steam API names + hidden flags, documented to match the Steam store backend config.
3. Add the **Steam bridge** in the Electron main process: renderer reports achievement-unlocked events via preload/IPC; main process calls Steamworks `SetAchievement`/`StoreStats`; local persistence of unlocked ids with later re-sync; graceful degradation without Steam.
4. **Wire Main Street** as the first consumer: a declarative mapping from the 12 challenge templates to Steam achievements, fired from the existing challenge-completion path.
5. Tests (mocked Steamworks session; headless unit tests for the engine layer) + documentation (README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` as needed).

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` (new) — generic achievement definitions + unlock registry + completion-event surface (no Steam dependency).
- `src/core-engine/index.ts` — barrel exports for the new module.
- `electron/steam-achievements.ts` (new) — achievement manifest (ids ↔ Steam API names) + Steamworks sync bridge.
- `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.ts` — IPC surface for achievement-unlock events from the renderer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` (or a new `MainStreetAchievements.ts`) — mapping of the 12 challenge templates to achievements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (engine layer, manifest matching) + mocked-Steamworks sync tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — Steam achievements workflow documentation.

## Related work

# Intake Brief: Electron Runtime Game Plugin Loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5)

## Problem Statement

The Electron launcher currently requires a rebuild to add new games — all games are statically imported and registered in `main.ts`. The producer wants a runtime plugin system so that a game can be added to an already-built launcher distribution by dropping in game artifacts and updating a manifest, without rebuilding the launcher itself.

## Users

- **Distribution operator** (primary) — Ships the Electron launcher and wants to add or update games post-build by placing game artifact directories and updating a manifest.
  - *Story:* As a distribution operator, I can drop a game's built artifacts into a `games/` directory and add a manifest entry, so that the launcher picks it up at startup without rebuilding.
- **Engine maintainer** — Ensures dynamically-loaded games are compatible with the core engine version in the launcher.
  - *Story:* As an engine maintainer, I can declare a required `coreEngineVersion` in a game's manifest, so that the launcher rejects incompatible games with a clear error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Runtime game discovery** — The Electron renderer reads a `games/manifest.json` from the content directory at startup, discovers each game's scene class, metadata (title, description, thumbnail), and registers it dynamically so it appears in the Game Selector alongside statically-registered games.
- **Core version compatibility check** — Each game declares a `coreEngineVersion` (semver range) in its manifest; the launcher checks compatibility at load time and skips incompatible games with a clear error message in the Game Selector UI.
- **Asset resolution** — Thumbnails and other game-specific assets are resolved relative to the game's artifact location (not relative to the launcher's `public/` directory).
- **Graceful degradation** — If the manifest is missing, malformed, or a game fails to load, the launcher continues with the statically-registered games and logs an error. Incompatible games are hidden from the selector but their presence is noted (e.g., "Incompatible game: X — requires core vY.Z").
- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the loader present (no regression for build-time presets).

## Constraints

- **Electron-only** — Web runtime plugin is explicitly out of scope.
- **Build-time presets** are handled in CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 (the parent epic); this is purely the runtime plugin phase.
- **Backwards compatible** — The existing static game registration (hardcoded imports in `main.ts`) must continue to work; the plugin system augments rather than replaces it.
- **No npm publication** of games — games are distributed as artifact directories (Vite library-mode ESM builds).
- **Shared dependencies** — Phaser and core-engine must be externalized (not bundled into game artifacts) to avoid duplication.

## Existing State

- `main.ts` (renderer entry): Static imports of every game scene + static `GAMES` array + Phaser scene registration. No dynamic loading.
- `electron/main.ts`: Loads the renderer from a resolved content directory. Has a `ContentDirectoryProvider` chain for content resolution (bundled → Steam DLC override), but no game discovery logic.
- `electron/launcher-config.ts` + `content-locator.ts`: Content directory resolution with provider chain. Extensible but game-discovery-aware.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`: Reads `GameEntry[]` from Phaser registry (`REGISTRY_KEY_GAMES`), renders the game selector grid.
- Parent epic CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 at `plan_complete` will introduce `configs/<preset>.json` for build-time game selection (F3 feature).

## Desired Change

- **Manifest schema**: Define a `games/manifest.json` format with entries containing `id`, `sceneKey`, `title`, `description`, `thumbnail` (relative path), `coreEngineVersion` (semver range), and `entry` (path to the game's ESM entry point).
- **Manifest loader**: A new module (e.g., `src/ui/GamePluginLoader.ts`) that reads the manifest from the content directory, validates entries, and returns a `GameEntry[]` array that merges with statically-registered games.
- **Version compatibility**: Use a semver range matcher (e.g., `semver.satisfies`) to check `coreEngineVersion` against the launcher's core engine version.
- **Dynamic scene loading**: For each compatible game, use `import()` to load the game's ESM entry point, extract the scene class, and register it with `scene.add(sceneKey, SceneClass)` before booting Phaser.
- **Asset paths**: Thumbnails are loaded from a path relative to the game's artifact directory (e.g., `games/my-game/assets/thumbnail.png`), resolved by the plugin loader.
- **Game Selector integration**: The Game Selector receives the merged list (static + dynamic) and renders them identically. Incompatible games are either hidden or shown with a disabled state and tooltip explaining the incompatibility.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/GamePluginLoader.ts` — **New file.** Reads manifest, validates entries, loads game chunks dynamically, returns merged `GameEntry[]`.
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` — Update to accept dynamically-loaded games; add UI for incompatible game indicators.
- `main.ts` — Update `preBoot` callback to call `GamePluginLoader.load()` and merge with static `GAMES`.
- `electron/main.ts` — May need to expose the resolved content directory path to the renderer (e.g., via `preload.cjs` → `window.TCE.contentDir`) so the plugin loader can find the manifest.
- `electron/preload.cjs` — Add preload bridge for `TCE.contentDir` if not already exposed.
- `package.json` — Add `semver` as a dependency (or use a lightweight alternative).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the `games/manifest.json` schema and plugin loading process.
- `AGENTS.md` — Add plugin loading pattern to the Game Architecture Best Practices section.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Dynamic import() in Electron renderer** — Loading ESM modules dynamically in the Electron renderer (Chromium context) may have path resolution quirks. *Mitigation:* Prototype early; use absolute paths resolved from the manifest's content directory.
- **Shared dependency bundling** — If games bundle their own Phaser/core-engine copies, the result is heavy and may cause class-identity issues (two Phaser instances). *Assumption:* Games are built as Vite library modules with `rollupOptions.external: ['phaser', '@core-engine/*']` so they rely on the launcher's bundled copies.
- **Thumbnail loading** — Electron's `file://` protocol may have CORS restrictions for loading images from `games/*/assets/`. *Mitigation:* Use `fs://` protocol or copy thumbnails to a shared asset location during game registration; or use `nativeImage` API in preload.
- **Scope creep** — Features like hot-reload of plugins, game updates, per-game settings panels, or web runtime support are natural follow-ons but are **out of scope**. *Mitigation:* Document them as linked follow-up opportunities.
- **Assumption:** The `games/` directory lives inside the content directory (resolved by `launcher-config.ts`), e.g., `<contentDir>/games/`.
- **Assumption:** `coreEngineVersion` uses semver ranges (e.g., `"~4.0.0"`) and compatibility is checked via major version (breaking changes) and minor/patch (non-breaking).
- **Assumption:** Games are built with Vite library mode, producing ESM chunks (e.g., `dist/index.js`) that export a `GameScene` class and a `GAME_INFO` object.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Where should the manifest live — in the content directory (`games/manifest.json`) or in Electron's userData (`~/Library/Application Support/TCE/plugins/manifest.json`)?" — Answer (producer, CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 planning session): "In the content directory, alongside game artifacts." Source: planning comment on CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17. Research: content directory is the game content root resolved by `launcher-config.ts`, so placing the manifest there keeps game artifacts and metadata together.
- Q: "Should dynamically-added games declare a required core version?" — Answer (producer, this session): "Yes — core-engine version." Source: existing description note.
- Q: "What happens to incompatible games in the Game Selector?" — Answer (assumption): "Hidden from the selector, with their incompatibility noted in error logs. Future work could add a disabled entry with a tooltip." Source: reasoned assumption from AC4 draft. *OPEN for producer confirmation.*
- Q: "Should the plugin loader run synchronously (blocking Phaser boot) or asynchronously (show a loading state)?" — Answer (assumption): "Asynchronously, with a brief loading overlay if needed. The `GamePluginLoader.load()` returns a Promise that resolves before the `preBoot` callback completes." Source: reasoned assumption for good UX. *OPEN for producer confirmation.*

## Problem

`rasteriseSvgToTexture()` in `src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` hard-codes a 4x oversampling factor:

```ts
const qualityScale = Math.max(4, dpr);
const targetW = Math.round(width * qualityScale);
```

Every card SVG is therefore rasterised at 4x its logical size (a 140x80 card becomes a 560x320 canvas) regardless of how large it is actually drawn. Consequences:

- The 64x64 art zone within that SVG occupies 256x256 device pixels, forcing the embedded bitmap to be upscaled 4x (see CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R for the complementary embedded-art fix).
- ~16x more texture memory and GPU upload bandwidth than the display actually needs.
- Texture cache keys encode the logical size + DPR, not the rendered size, so every card is over-allocated.

## Proposed change

Rasterise at the display native resolution: `qualityScale = dpr` (i.e. render at `width x dpr`), so textures are allocated at exactly the device pixels they occupy. Retain a small supersample (e.g. 1x) for the vector stroke/text quality if visual review shows artefacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `rasteriseSvgToTexture()` no longer hard-codes a 4x multiplier; the render resolution is derived from the display density (DPR)
2. Existing `SvgHelpers` unit/browser tests are updated to assert the new resolution contract
3. Card textures are allocated at `width * dpr` (verified by a test asserting canvas dimensions)
4. No visual regression in card text/vector stroke legibility (reviewed at DPR 1, 2 and 3)
5. Unit tests pass (`npm test -- --project unit`)
6. Build succeeds (`npm run build`)

## Interaction with CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R

The two fixes are complementary. Reducing the SVG rasterisation to native resolution lowers the required embedded-art resolution; raising the embedded art makes the card crisp at any rasterisation scale. Decide the final art resolution (64x64, 128x128 or 256x256) once this change lands.

## Open question (producer review)

Interpretation of "native resolution" in the request is ambiguous. This work item assumes it means "the display native resolution (DPR-matched)" rather than the 4x quality scale. If instead it means "generate the card SVG canvas at a higher intrinsic size (e.g. 560x320 native with a 256x256 art zone)", the ACs above should be rewritten. Confirm before implementing.

## Problem

`implement.py finish` removes the worktree and pushes the feature branch into `dev` **from the main checkout** (`repo_root`). The pre-push context-budget gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) measures the **working tree of the push source** — so when the commit being pushed changes `AGENTS.md`/thresholds, the main checkout is still at the old (breaching) dev state and the gate rejects the push, even though the pushed commit is compliant.

Observed while implementing CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ: `finish` passed build + full suite, committed `85ae7038`, then failed the push with `Context budget exceeded committed thresholds`. The commit had to be pushed manually from a worktree at the commit (`WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev`), where the gate measured the new files and passed without `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1`.

## Impact

Any commit that legitimately changes the startup context surface (e.g. an `AGENTS.md` edit) cannot be pushed by `implement.py finish` without a bypass, undermining the gate and forcing manual recovery.

## Options

1. `finish` pushes from the worktree (new files present) before removing it, rather than from the main checkout.
2. The hook measures the **pushed commit** (e.g. `git show <local-sha>:AGENTS.md`) instead of the working tree.
3. `finish` fast-forwards the local parent branch to the commit before pushing.

Discovered during CG-0MUFCL5N50023PHJ; recovered manually.

## Goal

Resolve game-specific assets (thumbnails and other files) relative to each game's artifact directory, and serve them safely to the Electron renderer under a packaged `file://`/asar build — realising AC3 (asset resolution).

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). `GameSelectorScene` currently loads `assets/<thumbnail>.png` from the launcher's own `public/` root; runtime games must instead resolve from `<contentDir>/games/<id>/…`. Direct `file://` image loads from arbitrary content dirs can hit CORS/canvas-taint and path issues, so a scoped custom protocol is introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Asset resolution** — Thumbnails and other game-specific assets are resolved relative to the game's artifact location (not relative to the launcher's `public/` directory).
- **Asset resolution** — A pure resolver `resolveGameAssetUrl(gameId, relativePath)` returns a `tce-games://<id>/<normalised-path>` URL, rejecting any path that escapes the game directory (`..`, absolute paths, `\0`).
- The Electron main process registers a `tce-games://` protocol (privileged/`standard` + `secure`) that resolves requests only inside `<contentDir>/games/`; requests outside that root return `404`/are denied.
- The protocol handler is Electron-free-unit-testable via an injectable file reader/resolver (no Electron import in the pure logic).
- MIME types are set for at least `.png`; unknown extensions are served as `application/octet-stream`.
- Unit tests cover the resolver (valid, traversal, encoded traversal) and the protocol path-resolution logic.

- Add `src/ui/game-asset-url.ts` with `resolveGameAssetUrl` + `resolveAssetFilePath(contentDir, requestUrl)`.
- Register the protocol in `electron/main.ts` before window creation (`protocol.handle`), reusing the resolver.
- Tests in `tests/ui/game-asset-url.test.ts` and `tests/electron/game-protocol.test.ts`.

- `src/ui/game-asset-url.ts`
- `electron/main.ts`
- `tests/ui/game-asset-url.test.ts`
- `tests/electron/game-protocol.test.ts`

## Goal

Wire the plugin loader into the Electron launcher boot path: await dynamic game discovery before Phaser boots, register discovered scenes, seed the merged catalogue, and degrade gracefully to the static catalogue on any failure.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). Realises AC1 (register discovered scenes), AC3 (assets via protocol from F3) and AC4 (graceful degradation). - **Graceful degradation** — If the manifest is missing, malformed, or a game fails to load, the launcher continues with the statically-registered games and logs an error. - `electron/main.ts` registers the `tce-games://` protocol before `createWindow()` and continues to load the renderer via `loadFile`.
- Unit/integration tests cover: no-Electron fallback, malformed manifest fallback, successful merge (appended scenes + entries), and protocol-registration wiring (via injectable/testable seams).

## Goal

Add the failing unit tests that pin the capacity-template contract (parent AC1–AC6) **before** the `HandView` fix lands, so the regression is captured as an executable specification.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Test-first item.

Today `HandView.computeCardPositions()` builds one row centred on the **current** `cards.length`, and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts that row; adding a card therefore re-centres every card and every outline. The fix (sibling item) will derive positions from `maxSlots`. These tests must be red against the current code and green once the fix lands.

The existing Phaser mock in `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` (mock `scene.add.rectangle` / `image` / `text`) is the harness to reuse; assert on `scene._rectangles` (outlines), `handView` sprites, and `outlineRects`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1: with `maxSlots` set, the set of outline slot positions for a given capacity is **identical** for a hand of 0, 1, … `maxSlots` cards (measured: the `outlineRects[i].x` for every `i` is unchanged across `setCards` of each size) — asserted as a unit test in `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`.
- Parent AC2: adding a card places it in the next empty slot to the right of the occupied run, and every already-placed card keeps its pre-add position (measured: for `addCard`, `sprite[i].x` before === after for all pre-existing `i`) — asserted for successive adds up to capacity and for successive `setCards` growth.
- Parent AC3: occupied outline slots still sit at the exact card position and rotation (`rect.x/y/rotation === sprite.x/y/rotation`), and extra capacity slots still render below every card — the CG-0MT6ER7YY003G680 invariant is preserved.
- Parent AC4: changing capacity (`setMaxSlots(n)`) re-lays the whole row and always yields exactly `n` slots; this is the only mutation that may move existing cards.
- Parent AC5: the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged from today's behaviour — `maxSlots` straight/arc slots centred on the hand centre — so an empty hand still shows the full capacity in the same place the cards will occupy.
- Parent AC6: unit tests verify AC 1–5, including a regression test that asserts positions do **not** move across successive `addCard`/`setCards` calls up to capacity, and that `setMaxSlots` does re-layout.
- Rotation/arc stability: per-card rotation and arc Y are derived from the capacity template, so they do not change when a card is added (assert `sprite.rotation` unchanged for pre-existing cards).
- `getInsertionPosition(i)` equals the rendered sprite position after inserting at `i` (guards the Main Street market→hand transfer).
- Over-capacity (transiently `cards.length > maxSlots`) is best-effort: the first `maxSlots` slots stay fixed, outlines stay capped at `maxSlots`, overflow cards continue to the right with the same step.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout (regression guard), and vertical cascade (already count-independent) is unchanged.
- Run via `npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` (unit profile).

- `tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts` — extend with the stability/regression cases (existing Phaser mock harness).
- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — read-only reference for the API under test.

## Goal

Fix the shared `HandView` so that, when `maxSlots` is set, card and outline positions derive from the hand's **capacity** rather than the current card count — adding a card never moves an existing card or slot.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Sibling test items add the failing unit and browser tests first.

Root cause: `computeCardPositions()` builds a row centred on `this.cards.length` (`layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })`), and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts it (plus appending extras). The empty-hand branch already lays out the desired fixed `maxSlots` row, so that row is the template to reuse. `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path all re-derive the row/rotation normalisation from the occupied positions and must move to the template as well. `setMaxSlots()` currently only rebuilds outlines and does not re-lay the cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1–AC5: implement the capacity-template behaviour — outline slot positions identical for a hand of 0…`maxSlots` cards; `addCard` fills the next slot right of the occupied run while pre-existing card positions are unchanged; occupied outlines still match card `x/y/rotation` with extras below every card; `setMaxSlots(n)` is the only mutation that re-lays the row and always yields exactly `n` slots; the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged (same centred straight/arc row the cards will occupy).
- Add a shared private helper in `src/ui/HandView.ts` that derives the `maxSlots` template with the existing `layoutCardPositions` maths (gap = `spacing - cardWidth`, `centerX`, `maxWidth` compression, `arcRadius` Y) and the template-span rotation normalisation; recompute from current options on each use (no stale cache).
- `computeCardPositions()` horizontal returns the first `cards.length` template positions; over-capacity cards continue with the template step to the right (best-effort, no re-centring).
- `getInsertionPosition(index)` returns the template position at `index` (first `maxSlots`; template step beyond), so Market→hand transfer animations land exactly on the resting card.
- `_computeOutlineSlots()` derives all `count` slots from the same template (occupied slots ghost the card's **actual** sprite rotation, extras keep `depth = index - 0.5 - count`), replacing the per-count ghosting/extension branch.
- Rotation and arc normalisation in `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path use the template span when `maxSlots` is set, so per-card rotation is also stable across adds.
- `setMaxSlots(maxSlots)` re-lays the cards (calls `applyLayout()`), not just the outlines.
- Capacity-driven layout is keyed on `maxSlots !== undefined`, independent of `showPositionOutlines`; toggling outlines never moves cards.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout; vertical cascade keeps `baseY + i * spacing` and is not regressed.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` is reused unchanged.
- The sibling unit and browser test items pass (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`, `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, `sortCards()` animated path, `setMaxSlots()`.

# Feature: Ship the ToneForge runtime synth module everywhere (commit it)

## Goal (user story)

As a player/tester running TCE in **any** environment — the launcher dev server,
a game-repo dev server, the built `dist/` (GitHub Pages), or the Electron
bundle — Main Street's ToneForge-backed synthesis audio works out of the box,
without anyone having to install the `tf` CLI or run `npm run tf:generate`
first.

## Context

Today the runtime synth module is generated on demand and never shipped:

- `scripts/tf-generate-synths.sh` writes `build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs`
  (and a metadata module + WAVs + JSON) and **hard-fails** (`exit 1`) if the
  `tf` CLI is not on `PATH`.
- `build/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:15`) and Vite only copies `public/` into
  `dist/`, so the artefact is reachable on the dev server (which serves
  repo-root files) but **absent from `dist/` and the Electron bundle**.
- The runtime pre-checks `/build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` and,
  when missing, logs `[MainStreet] ToneForge synth module not found …`
  (`src/tf/mainStreetTfModule.ts`).
- The decision recorded in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (§ToneForge Audio Generation) and
  `docs/the-build/audio.md` is explicitly **"we do not commit generated tf
  artifacts"** — this work item reverses that for the runtime module.
- CI never installs ToneForge, so generating at build time cannot work there.

The generated runtime module is **static JavaScript** (hard-coded Tone.js
factories) whose only runtime dependency is `tone`, which is already a shipped
dependency. It therefore does not need `tf`, WAVs, or network access at runtime.

## Proposed approach (confirm during planning)

1. Make the generated **runtime synth module** a source-controlled artefact so
   it is present in every checkout and copied into every build. Likely:
   generate/commit it at a path the runtime already serves
   (`public/build/tf-synths/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` in the launcher keeps
   the existing `/build/tf-synths/…` URL unchanged), or place it with the
   Main Street game assets and compose it via
   `repo-layout.json → gameAssets` (CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA), updating the default
   URL.
2. Make `scripts/tf-generate-synths.sh` **fail-open**: a missing `tf` CLI is a
   warning/regeneration hint, never a build failure. `npm run build`/`dev` must
   not depend on `tf` and must not be changed to run generation.
3. Decide what is committed vs generated: commit the runtime module (and
   evaluate the metadata module); keep WAV/JSON generated output out of source
   control.
4. Update the docs to state which artefact is committed and how to regenerate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Clean checkout, no `tf`, no generation:** with the `tf` CLI absent and
   `npm run tf:generate` never run, `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run dev` serves the
   runtime synth module at the exact URL `loadMainStreetTfModule()` requests,
   Main Street logs **no** `ToneForge synth module not found` warning, and
   synth-mapped SFX are active.
2. **Shipped build:** `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build` emits the module into
   `dist/` at the same URL path, and serving `dist/` (e.g. `npm run preview`)
   loads it with no warning. Same for `npm run build:electron`.
3. **Deterministic + single source of truth:** the committed module is the file
   the runtime loads; running `npm run tf:generate` (when `tf` is available)
   regenerates exactly that artefact with no drift, and the absence of `tf`
   never fails `npm run build` or `npm run dev`.
4. **Test coverage:** a unit test asserts the runtime default URL resolves to an
   on-disk artefact that is included in the public/build output, and that the
   module exports `TF_RUNTIME_MODULE`/`factories` including the expected keys
   (`card-draw`, `card-slide`, `card-place`, `card-discard`,
   `card-coin-collect`, `ui-notification-chime`, `card-table-ambience`,
   `construction-hammer`, `construction-saw`, `construction-lite-hammer`,
   `construction-lite-saw`, `crowd-cheer`).
5. **Docs:** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` §ToneForge Audio Generation and
   `docs/the-build/audio.md` no longer claim the runtime module is uncommitted;
   they state which artefact is source-controlled and how to regenerate it.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Committing WAV or JSON generation output (binary/large) is out of scope.
- If the module must also be present in the **standalone `tce-main-street`
  repo**, that is a cross-repo follow-up; record it as a child/spin-off if the
  chosen placement does not cover it.

## Related

- Reverses the "do not commit generated tf artifacts" decision in
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `docs/the-build/audio.md`.
- Prior work: CG-0MOIY2VV200658OX (TF output spike + spec, open questions #2/#4),
  CG-0MOIY3MSR008EH0I (npm script + docs), CG-0MOIXHOWP003Y6E0 (runtime
  synthesis).
- Sibling asset composition: CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA.
- Discovered-from: CG-0MUKYCG9L00587FA.

## Goal

Update the CPU-contention mitigation guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` to match
the deterministic game-loop stepping pattern now used by Main Street's
contention-prone browser tests, replacing the stale `requestAnimationFrame`
(`waitForFrames()`) guidance that no longer matches any helper in the tree.

## Context

Discovered during the `tce-main-street` audit of **MS-0MUE2U21C0007BKL**
(`upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` contention flake). The fix for that item
(shipped as `dc04fb9`, `5f951d5`, `fce85ee`, `48d35b9`, `6ab3274` in
`tce-main-street`) replaced the rAF-based gesture waiting with direct
`TimeStep.step(time)` stepping:

- `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` — `stepGame()` drives
  the Phaser loop synchronously instead of awaiting animation frames.
- `tests/main-street/market-deal-in.browser.test.ts` — same pattern.

The audit verdict for MS-0MUE2U21C0007BKL is `Ready to close: No`; AC2
(documentation) is `partial` solely because `docs/DEVELOPER.md:507-527`
still tells authors to `await two requestAnimationFrame callbacks
(waitForFrames())` before the first `mousedown`, and to poll frame-gated waits
on `requestAnimationFrame`. No `waitForFrames()` helper exists anywhere in the
tree, so the guidance is misleading.

## Scope

- In scope: the **CPU-contention mitigation (unit and browser tests)** section
  of `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (around lines 430-620), specifically the two bullets
  at ~507-527.
- Out of scope: the browser-stage wall-clock bound, which is already accurate
  (`docs/DEVELOPER.md` ~642-647).

## Suggested change

Rewrite the two bullets to describe the current pattern:

1. Flush pending interactive insertions deterministically by stepping the
   Phaser game loop (`TimeStep.step(time)`), rather than awaiting rAF. Under
   full-suite contention rAF may be starved for seconds, so the game loop —
   and therefore `InputPlugin.preUpdate`, which flushes `_pendingInsertion`
   into `_list` — may never run.
2. Poll frame-gated waits by stepping the loop on each poll (with a `setTimeout`
   yield), so the waits make progress even when no animation frame is granted.
3. Note the synchronous teardown helper
   (`@core-tests/helpers/phaserCanvasPool`) used by the game suites.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `docs/DEVELOPER.md` no longer references `waitForFrames()` or prescribes
   awaiting rAF before a gesture; it describes the `stepGame`/`TimeStep.step`
   pattern with a reference to the tests that use it.
2. The guidance matches the code in the sibling `tce-main-street` repo
   (`tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts`,
   `tests/main-street/market-deal-in.browser.test.ts`).
3. The core documentation gate (context budget / docs checks) stays green.

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want the CI-built Windows installer
(`TCE-Setup-<version>.exe` from the `Package Windows Binary` workflow) promoted to
a GitHub Release automatically as part of the release process, so I do not have
to remember to run `/skill:release-windows` manually after every `dev`→`main`
release.

## Context

- `.github/workflows/package.yml` builds the installer on push to `main` and on
  tag `v*`, smoke-tests the packaged binary, and uploads it as the
  `tce-windows-installer` workflow artifact — but it never calls `gh release
  create`, so no GitHub Release is produced automatically.
- `.pi/skills/release-windows/` (CG-0MSQ6MV7N0085V9R, completed) is the
  **manual** path: it promotes the latest successful artifact to a **draft**
  GitHub Release with `CHANGELOG.md` notes, and the operator publishes the draft.
- `/skill:ship release` bumps the version, creates/pushes the tag `v<semver>`
  (ancestor of `origin/main`) and merges `dev`→`main`, then verifies the tag
  before closing work items.
- Gap: the promotion is agent-invoked and easy to miss; a release can ship the
  Pages site + workflow artifact while the GitHub Release never appears.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Automatic promotion** — After `dev`→`main` is released (tag `v*` pushed),
  the Windows installer is promoted to a GitHub Release with no manual skill
  invocation.
- **Draft, not published** — The created release is a **draft** (operator
  publishes it in the GitHub UI). It attaches `TCE-Setup-<version>.exe`, uses the
  matching `CHANGELOG.md` section as release notes (falling back to
  `--generate-notes` when absent), and reuses the existing `v<version>` tag —
  never overwriting an existing release or tag.
- **Idempotent** — Re-running promotion for a version that already has a release
  is a no-op that reports the existing release URL.
- **Non-blocking failure** — A failed promotion (no successful
  `Package Windows Binary` run, missing artifact, missing/insufficient `gh`
  auth) does not fail the Pages deploy and is surfaced with a clear message
  (workflow annotation / job summary).
- **Single source of truth for the version** — The release version is derived
  from the installer filename / `package.json` (`electron-builder.yml`
  `artifactName`), consistent with the existing `release-windows` helper.
- **Tests** — The promotion logic is covered by automated tests (workflow
  dry-run and/or unit tests around the promotion helper); the existing
  `tests/release-windows/` suite continues to pass.
- **Documentation updated** — `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (packaging/release section)
  and the release-process docs state that the GitHub Release is produced
  automatically; the `release-windows` skill is updated to reflect the
  automated path while remaining the documented manual fallback.

## Out of scope

- Linux/macOS binary promotion (Windows only, as today).
- Steam upload integration.
- Auto-**publishing** releases (the draft remains the operator approval gate).

## Assumptions

- Interpreted as **automating/integrating** the existing promotion into the
  release pipeline rather than a one-off manual promotion. If a one-off was
  intended, this item can be closed by running `/skill:release-windows` on the
  current version.
- Draft (not published) remains the correct approval model, matching the
  existing skill.
